requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with pagination

guide.summary: Use a user-owned GitLab OAuth application with the read_api scope and the authorization code flow with PKCE. Each connected person approves access, and the app then lists project issues through GET /projects/:id/issues with pagination. Setup is documented. Customer-distribution review and customer-admin approval are not documented in the supplied sources, so they remain unknown and are not part of the first test.

findings.title: Request read_api to read issues in accessible projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. Use it for the GET issue listing. No narrower issue-specific scope is documented in the supplied sources.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.

findings.detail: The authorization page asks the signed-in user to approve the app's access. The app should not assume another person's approval.

findings.title: Project access depends on the connected person's membership
findings.detail: Private project issue listing requires credentials. The endpoint returns only projects the authenticated user can access, so the test account needs access to a representative project.

evidence.quote: If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.
Lists all projects on the instance accessible to the authenticated user. Unauthenticated requests return only public projects with a limited subset of attributes.

findings.title: Pagination uses offset by default, with keyset recommended for consecutive pages
findings.detail: Issue responses return 20 results by default. The endpoint supports offset and keyset pagination, and keyset is recommended for consecutive pages. Keyset support depends on the GitLab version.

evidence.quote: Responses in this API are paginated and return 20 results by default.
This endpoint supports both offset-based and keyset-based pagination. You should use keyset-based

findings.title: Target GitLab instance must be identified
findings.detail: The GitLab offering can be GitLab.com, Self-Managed, or Dedicated. Each customer's instance host must be known before the API request can be sent.

steps.doneWhen: The application shows a client ID and lists read_api as its only scope.

steps.title: Test reading issue titles from one accessible project
steps.detail: Call the project issues endpoint with the OAuth bearer token. Expect a JSON array of issue objects, and read the title field from each item. Boundary check: confirm the token scope in the GitLab token details is read_api and the outgoing request log contains only this GET.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a 200 JSON array and the issue titles are readable.

evidence.quote: Lists all issues for a specified project.
json [ { "state" : "opened" ,
--header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \

steps.title: Test pagination of issue titles with a second page
steps.detail: Request page 2 with a small page size, and compare titles against page 1. Boundary check: keep the request to GET and verify no POST, PUT, or DELETE appears in the request log.
steps.doneWhen: Page 2 returns a different set of issues and the next-page headers are read correctly.

evidence.quote: Responses in this API are paginated and return 20 results by default.
--url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/9/issues/8/notes?per_page=3&page=2" The response is:
link : <https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/8/issues/8/notes?page=1&per_page=3>; rel="prev", <https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/8/issues/8/notes?page=3&per_page=3>; rel="next",

steps.title: Verify no write requests are sent
steps.detail: Review the app's outgoing requests from the test. Boundary check: confirm only GET requests to the issues endpoint occurred. Do not send a create, update, or delete request to test this.
steps.doneWhen: The request log for the test shows only GET requests and no issue write calls.
